front: Why does keeping one path per tag suffice?
back: Markov property: the future depends on the past only through the current tag, so a dominated partial path can never be part of the optimum.
Viterbi uses max and returns the best path; forward uses sum and returns $P(x)$.
B-X begins an entity of type X, I-X continues it, O is outside. Turns NER into sequence labelling.
Avoids underflow; zero probability becomes $-\infty$, harmless for the max.
HMM is generative ($P(x,t)$, word depends on its tag only). Linear-chain CRF is discriminative ($P(t\mid x)$) with arbitrary features; decoding is still Viterbi.
Entity-level precision, recall and F1: exact span and type must match. Token accuracy is inflated by O tokens.

front: Why are unknown words a problem for HMM taggers?
back: Their emission probability is 0 for every tag; fix with smoothing, an UNK class or suffix/shape features.
